<!-- pr-reviewer: 8d7a8254d129c761d9d75d38c89482629089c8d8 -->
**Review: clean (read, not built).** Head 8d7a8254d. Label: merge-ready. P3 stands (fixes #2944).

What the change does:
- `wall_lean(frame, depth)` computes the plan move of an upright wall from the operation frame only. No frame or an upright frame gives zero. A tool axis in the world XY plane gives `None`, and no loop is then exempt. This closes #2944: a 1 mm bevel on one side and an equal undercut lip on the other moved the whole outline, but no upright frame leans a wall, and the #2887 refusal now holds.
- `partly_bevelled` cuts each top segment at the foot of each wall vertex inside it, and judges each piece. The overhang and the sharp length read apart.
- The app caller (`material_source.rs`) passes the frame lean into `chamfer_ride_loops`; the signature change reaches one call site, and `mod.rs` re-exports `chamfer_wall_lean`.

Checks I made:
- `wall_lean` guards the divide: `axis[2].abs() > 1e-9` and a finiteness check before it returns a lean. No unchecked float path in the new index or bounds math; `seg` clamps `t`.
- `leans` now tests each segment end and mid against both rings, in both directions. The old centroid move is gone; the test `the_wall_lean_is_the_frames_own` pins the frame cases.
- Test pins: `an_upright_bevel_beside_an_equal_undercut_lip_still_refuses` (#2944), `a_wall_leaning_in_the_frame_is_not_a_modelled_chamfer` and `a_moved_outline_with_one_side_bevelled_still_refuses` (#2936 fixture kept), `a_loop_bevelled_on_one_side_refuses_with_an_extra_vertex_too`. The refusal messages name the point and tell the user to break the edges.
- `chamfer_ride.rs` is 265 lines and the tests moved to their own file: the 400-line rule is served, not just kept.
- Decision doc `docs/decisions/2944-chamfer-lean-frame.md` records the choice; the 2936 doc is updated to match.
- No safety rule was dropped: a partly bevelled loop still refuses by name on every path.

Note: this is safety-floor geometry (a gouge-adjacent refusal), so the merge batch gives it a read-only second review at the safety tier before the merge.

Author's gate: quick gate, 136 steps green on the final head (PR body). Runner m3 was busy; no pr-test run for this head. Not built here.
